How to make Korean cucumber Kimchi (takes less than 30 min)

Hi, I wanted to share a beginner’s recipe to make Korean Cucumber Kimchi at home! In Korea, we usually see this at restaurants as a side-dish. It goes well with other meat-dishes or simply with some rice. Note, there are many types of Kimchi variations – this one does not go under a fermentation process. So it’s fast, simple and doesn’t require too many ingredients to make!

 Ingredients (Serving size for 2):
  • Cucumbers - 3
  • Vinegar  – 3 teaspoon
  • Korean red chili flakes  – 2.5 teaspoon
  • Sugar – 2.5 teaspoon
  • Soy Sauce – 1 teaspoon
  • Minced Garlic – 1 teaspoon
  • Sesame oil – 1 teaspoon
  • Sesame seeds – Optional, garnish
 Directions
  • Wash all three cucumbers and skin each cucumber with a peeler (Do not peel-off all of the skin, rather make uneven peels) (Watch the video for visual guide)
  • Chop cucumbers into half inch circles
  • Pour salt onto the cucumbers and give them a good mix with your hands to coat thoroughly. Set the cucumbers aside for 30 minutes and they will slowly release water. Rinse them off and get rid of excess water.
  • For the marinade: Thoroughly mix vinegar, Korean red chili powder, sugar, soy sauce, and minced garlic in a bowl.
  • Dress the cucumbers with the marinade. (Get in there with you hands and coat all of it!)
 What else?
  • Refrigerate – taste better when served chilled
